title: Could a shark end up in your local swimming pool?
caption: Could a shark end up in your local swimming pool? 🦈🏊 We checked every way in. #shark #bullshark #flood #science #shorts | Music: "Dark Moment" by E. Erkut (CC BY 3.0)

scenes.text: {{q}}Could a shark end up in your local pool? ||0.2|| {{check}}Let's check every way in.
{{w1}}Way one: the pipes. ||0.2|| {{cm}}They're ten centimetres wide. ||0.2|| {{not}}A shark is not.
{{w2}}Way two: the sea. ||0.2|| {{salt}}Great whites need salt water. ||0.2|| {{dead}}Dead end.
{{bull}}But bull sharks swim up rivers. ||0.2|| {{amazon}}Thousands of kilometres up the Amazon.
{{w3}}Way three: floods. ||0.2|| {{street}}Bull sharks have been filmed in flooded streets. ||0.3|| {{fake}}And no: the famous shark on the highway photo is fake.
{{golf}}In Australia, a flood left bull sharks in a golf course lake. ||0.2|| {{years}}For seventeen years.
{{so}}So: a flooded river, an outdoor pool, a bull shark. ||0.3|| {{drop}}When the water drops, it's stuck. ||0.3|| {{guard}}Then the lifeguard has a very strange morning.
{{gw}}Great white: no. ||0.2|| {{bs}}Bull shark: possible. ||0.3|| {{safe}}If your street floods, stay out of the water.
{{who}}Comment: would you still go swimming? ||0.3|| {{loop}}So if anyone asks you:
